draft.title: Legal and political factors
card: Legal factors are the laws a business must follow. Political factors are the decisions and policies of governments, which can lead to new laws or rules.
A new business must register. In Australia it usually needs an Australian Business Number (ABN) and a business name, and it must register for tax such as GST once its sales pass a set level.

Other laws set standards. Workplace health and safety laws protect workers. Consumer law, such as the Australian Consumer Law, requires businesses to be honest and to sell goods that work as promised.
A business cannot change these rules, but it can plan for them. Rules can change after an election, so owners watch for new laws that add costs or limit what they can sell.
draft.remember: Governments make the rules, and a business must plan to follow them.

a.q: Which example shows a political factor affecting a new business?
opts: A new government changes the rules for small business tax
A café owner chooses a shop on a busy street
A rival opens a café across the road
A supplier offers a discount on coffee beans
a.why: A government decision about tax is a political factor, and it can lead to a new rule the business must follow. The shop location is a choice the owner makes, and the rival and supplier belong to the business's own dealings with other firms.
a.clue: Which one comes from a government decision?

b.q: Jon sells handmade candles online from Geelong. A customer's candle melts badly and does not work as promised. Which type of law covers this?
opts: Consumer law, which requires goods to work as promised
Workplace safety law, which protects people at work
Registration law, which sets up a business name
Tax law, which sets how much GST is owed
b.why: Consumer law protects buyers and requires goods to work as promised, so it applies to a faulty candle. Workplace safety law is tempting because a candle can be a hazard, but it protects workers, not buyers.
b.clue: Who is being protected here, the worker or the buyer?

a.best: A new government changes the rules for small business tax

b.best: Consumer law, which requires goods to work as promised

problems.detail: The remember line says a business 'must plan to follow' the rules, but the card says a business 'can plan for them'. This 'must' overstates the card.

The right option repeats the stem's words 'work as promised' ('does not work as promised' / 'requires goods to work as promised'), so a student can match the phrase without knowing which law protects buyers.

The card says a new business 'usually needs' a business name. In Australia, registering a business name is only required when trading under a name other than the owner's own name, so students may think every business must register one.
